title: Dating Lies the World Taught You
paragraphs:
Dating Lies the World Taught You
The relationship advice everyone applauds may be preparing your heart for heartbreak—until Jesus rewrites the story.
There is a generation that knows how to swipe but struggles to surrender.
A generation that has mastered attraction but forgotten covenant.
A generation drowning in relationship advice while starving for biblical wisdom.
We were taught that love is something you "fall into."
Scripture teaches that love is someone you choose to become.
We were taught to chase chemistry.
God calls us to pursue Christlikeness.
We were told to find "the one."
Jesus calls us to become someone faithful enough to love the one He gives.
Some of the deepest scars people carry today were not caused by strangers.
They were left by people who once promised forever.
And perhaps the greatest tragedy is that many of those wounds happened while both people sincerely believed they were following what the world called "love."
If you have ever wondered why relationships today often leave people emptier instead of fuller...
Why loneliness exists even inside dating relationships...
Why people keep repeating the same painful cycles...
This article may expose more than you expected.
Some lies only lose their power when truth is allowed to linger.
Long before social media influencers, dating coaches, dating apps, relationship podcasts, and viral videos existed, the Creator already defined love.
The Bible never presents dating as entertainment.
It presents relationships as preparation for covenant.
While modern dating as we know it does not explicitly appear in Scripture, the principles governing purity, wisdom, faithfulness, holiness, self-control, sacrifice, and marriage are everywhere.
The problem is not merely that culture created new methods.
The problem is that culture also created new definitions.
One of the biggest lies ever believed is this:
"If it feels right, it must be right."

The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly use the word לֵב (lev), meaning "heart." In biblical thought, the heart is not merely the seat of emotions but the centre of one's will, desires, mind, and moral direction.
"The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?"
This is not saying emotions are evil.
It is saying emotions are fallen.
Jesus never taught His disciples to follow their hearts.
He taught them to deny themselves.
The Greek text of Luke 9:23 reads:
But it places a burden on another human being that only God was designed to carry.
Only Christ completes what sin shattered.
"And you have been filled in Him."
καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι (kai este en autō peplērōmenoi)
"You have been made complete in Him."
Otherwise marriage becomes idolatry disguised as intimacy.
But fire without boundaries burns houses down.
Biblical love is not driven by uncontrolled emotion.
When Paul describes love in 1 Corinthians 13, he never mentions butterflies.
Those qualities survive long after attraction changes.
The Greek word used for love throughout this chapter is ἀγάπη (agapē).
"If they love you, they'll never hurt you."
Yet God's grace continued rewriting broken stories.
Relationships do not survive because people are perfect.
They survive because repentance remains possible.
But because Christ's cross is greater.
Perhaps the most dangerous dating lie today is this:
The New Testament repeatedly uses the Greek word:
It includes every sexual practice outside God's design for the covenant of marriage between one man and one woman.
This is not because God is anti-pleasure.
It is because He is pro-holiness.
God never designed intimacy to be separated from covenant.
"Give your covenant because your body already has immeasurable value."
Perhaps no generation has compared relationships more than ours.
Social media has convinced millions that everyone else's love story is perfect.
Wedding highlights hide years of sanctification.
The tenth commandment still speaks today.
Because comparison eventually convinces you to abandon blessings God already gave.
Unrepentant sin should never be ignored.
But modern culture often uses this phrase to justify abandoning relationships whenever sacrifice becomes inconvenient.
Biblical marriage was never built upon convenience.
Jesus compared His relationship with the Church to marriage.
And He remained faithful even when His Bride failed Him repeatedly.
The world teaches you to ask:
The Gospel teaches you to ask:
"Am I becoming more like Christ because of this relationship?"
That question changes who you pursue.
It changes how you leave unhealthy relationships.
It changes how you enter healthy ones.
Perhaps you are reading this carrying regrets.
Maybe your past relationships left guilt.
Maybe purity feels impossible to recover.
Maybe shame whispers that you've gone too far.
The Bible never says your past gets the final word.
The woman caught in adultery expected condemnation.
The Samaritan woman carried broken relationships.
She became one of the first evangelists.
Rahab's scandal became part of Messiah's family line.
David's failures did not erase God's covenant.
Peter's denial became the backdrop for restoration.
Because this has always been God's story.
But redeeming those who truly repent.
That is why our message has always been:
If you have believed the world's dating lies, today can become the beginning of a different story.
Grace is not permission to continue sinning.
Grace is God's power to become someone new.
Perhaps your greatest relationship breakthrough will not happen because you finally meet the right person.
Perhaps it will happen because you finally surrender to the right Saviour.
Everything changes when Christ becomes your first love.
If this article exposed something hidden in your heart, don't simply move on.
Not to shame them, but because truth shared in love can become the beginning of restoration.
There may come a day when your emotions become louder than your convictions, and you will need to return to God's Word instead of the world's opinions.
Because one shared article may become someone else's answered prayer.
